newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa approves sale of state leisure company.
newsitem.headline: South Africa approves sale of state leisure company.

text.p: The South African government has formally approved the sale of state-run leisure group Aventura and is now seeking a privatisation adviser, a spokesman for the Ministry of Public Enterprises said on Wednesday.
He declined to give a timetable for the sale of the concern, although local newspapers speculated it could be completed by the end March.
Tenders for the sale of company -- which runs resorts around the country -- would be issued following the appointment of an adviser.
Aventura reported its first an operating profit in the year to August 1996, but management and the government believe the concern is badly in need of recapitalsiation.
Several local concerns are thought to be interested in acquiring the concern.
Aventura is one of seven public sector corporations Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau has said will be at least partly privatised by the end of 1997.
Sigcau said late last month that Aventura, Sun Air, mining group Alexcor and transport group Autonet would be fully privatised.
Strategic equity stakes are to be sold in telecommunications utility Telkom, the Airports Company which runs South Africa's major airports and forestry group Safcol.
South African Airways, the national carrier, is to seek a foreign equity partner by the middle of next year.
